title: Prove all-length terminal separation and exhibit two-axis path cancellation
body:
This proves an all-length obstruction for the actual coded terminal family: adding distinct fresh stages cannot produce a decoder with a constant number of scalar ADDs. It also gives an exact two-path cancellation when the interface has two shared central axes. **The complete kappa calculation is unchanged; no new supplier or higher kappa is claimed.**

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/256126eeb1607c0bf52996c3d90490f2b786b94a/research/fresh-stage-code-separation/PROOF.md), [exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/256126eeb1607c0bf52996c3d90490f2b786b94a/research/fresh-stage-code-separation/RESULT.json) and [marker certificates](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/256126eeb1607c0bf52996c3d90490f2b786b94a/research/fresh-stage-code-separation/MARKERS.json) contain the result and evidence.

For any fixed `k >= 1`, any order of distinct stages, and any nonzero integer stage powers, one common binary axis and eight private axes per stage give `ADDs >= max(0, 2f - 24k)`. This permits cross-owner scalar mixing, arbitrary owned workspace, and coefficients and monomial maps that depend on tensor width `f`. The linear instruction schedule must be independent of input values. The proof separates the binary map of every owner path, then isolates one term by coordinate contractions. Owner coefficients are applied once, outside tensor powers.

Short certificates strengthen the bound to `ADDs >= max(0, 2f - 6)` for **all sixteen negative-output banks** in the [saved caller](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/coded-native-caller/GAUGE.json), including its eighteen-stage bank. Do not add these sixteen bounds together. The previous two-stage bound retains its better constant for its two named banks.

With two shared axes, `L R = (L H)(H R)` gives distinct local paths with the same signed operator. The actual owner coefficients `+1/4` and `-1/4` then cancel at every tensor width. The proof specifies every map. This is a two-path construction, not a complete 112-owner provider. The extra central axis, remaining owners, targets and restoration still need a complete paid bill. A simple shared-axis screen on the unchanged source did not cancel the tested block; it is recorded as a bounded negative experiment.

Validation uses Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fresh-stage-code-separation
```

Expected final scientific marker:

```text
PASS_ALL_LENGTH_FRESH_STAGE_SEPARATION_NO_NEW_KAPPA
```

Both registered normal/optimized checks pass: 57,344 signed normalizer entries, all 12,544 code-polynomial entries, all 12,656 two/three-stage paths, 12,654 literal killing markers, both directions of the short-marker dynamic program, all sixteen banks, and repeated-stage/two-center controls. The marker proposer reproduces the saved bytes. Committed-byte and official export checks pass; both modes also pass in a read-only Git-free export. Five optimized mutation runs reject changed source bytes, an empty marker, a repeated stage, a wrong Q orientation, and a typed receipt change. [Hosted verification](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40041767797) passed for head `256126eeb1607c0bf52996c3d90490f2b786b94a`.

The unbounded theorem rests on its written induction. These checks share source data and elementary matrix code; independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is not claimed. No complete producer, native/outer/compiler admission, selected cold replay, Lean, Docker or optional full-history check was run. The checkout is shallow. Paid decoders, width-dependent scalar work, correlated saved histories, repeated stages, and changed recursive target contracts remain outside the obstruction.

Base: canonical main `1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4`, priority 7. Only the new scoped package changes. The frozen [code A](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/coded-native-caller/CODE.json) and [signed normalizers](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/coded-native-caller/NORMALIZERS.json) are copied byte-exactly. [Source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/256126eeb1607c0bf52996c3d90490f2b786b94a/research/fresh-stage-code-separation/SOURCES.json) retain exact copied bytes and notices. The [canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4930#discussioncomment-19156145) separates this proof from active caller and frame work. The selected conditional kappa remains 0.0030217758.

Credit @dillona for [PR #4933](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4933)'s physical code, signed normalizers and caller; @1337isnot1337 for [PR #5065](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5065)'s [two-stage proof and open longer-product question](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/two-stage-coded-terminal/PROOF.md); and @Dugongue for [PR #4929](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4929)'s center-free code. @intqwq (Cao Yifan), @zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman and the retained native/controller lineage remain credited in the [source notice](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/research/coded-native-caller/NOTICE). The code spectrum and one-stage four-point formula are predecessor results. New work by @aliromman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
